--- title: "[StepImputeMode]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Impute missing values with the column mode (most frequent value). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_impute_mode.py#L119-L239){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepImputeMode(columns, id=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each selected column has its nulls filled in place with that column's mode. Mode imputation is for categorical columns (it accepts ``Categorical``/``Enum``/``String``, not numeric dtypes) and is dtype-preserving — the fill value is an observed level of the column. A column that is entirely null at fit time has no mode; it is left unchanged (not dropped) with a warning, and passes through ``transform`` untouched. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Selector]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns to impute. Accepts a single column name, a list of names, a shoez selector such as ``Selectors.nominal_predictors()`` (see `Selectors` for the full set), or a narwhals or polars selector (``narwhals.selectors.string()``, ``polars.selectors.string()``). Selectors are resolved against the frame's schema when the recipe is fitted, so the same selector works on any backend. Only categorical columns are meaningful here. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"impute_mode"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The null is filled in place with the column mode (the most frequent observed level): ::: {#99e3db9c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame( {"city": pd.Series(["NYC", "LA", "NYC", None], dtype="category")} ) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
city
0 NYC
1 LA
2 NYC
3 NaN
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#d5d4cdc1 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepImputeMode(s.nominal_predictors())) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_impute_mode(select(role='predictor', type=(String, Categorical, Enum))) [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` finds the most frequent observed level: ::: {#dc601a8a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 1 columns — 1 predictor Steps: step_impute_mode(city) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` fills the nulls in place: ::: {#08bf0091 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
city
0 NYC
1 LA
2 NYC
3 NYC
``` ::: :::
